author: Kodao Productions
title: A supporter asks: ‘Why Is Leni Welcoming Israel?’
content:
By

 Pia Montalban




I have a question about Leni Robredo’s recent meeting with Israeli Ambassador Dana Kursh.




It is not a question I raise lightly. And it is not a question I raise because I have suddenly become an opponent of Leni Robredo.




I voted for her in 2022. I even campaigned for her in Tarlac, in the middle of that sea of pink, alongside Aeta communities. But I was never a full-fledged Kakampink. I still am not.




I supported her because, given the choices before us in 2022, there was a political calculation to make. I do not want a Marcos to return to Malacanang.




I decided to gamble. I gambled that a Robredo presidency could create more political space for the demands of workers, peasants, indigenous peoples, human rights defenders and other communities I worked with. I gambled that there would be more room to organize, to criticize, to make demands, to defend people, and to push our calls into government.




But a gamble is not surrender. People gamble on a candidate. I belong to those who did not gamble away their principles. That distinction matters to me. Because I had already questioned Leni long before I campaigned for her.




I had questions before I wore pink




In 2021, when

 Leni expressed support for the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict

, I was deeply troubled.




For me, this was never an abstract policy quest

author: Kodao Productions
title: Love, death, struggle: Palestinian refugee couple hopes to return to Gaza
content:
Filipina Fatima Cargolio met her Palestinian husband Naji Al-Abdala while both were working at Al-Ain three decades ago. They had a daughter and a son in the UAE before eventually moving to Gaza, Naji’s homeland.




“Life was good for us in Gaza. We were operating a store near Al-Quds University selling spices, chocolates and biscuits,” Fatima recalled. She said they had their own house, a farm and their children were enrolled in the university.




Everything drastically changed when October 7, 2023 came, Fatima said. She counted 30 drone attacks in their neighborhood, targeting the police headquarters nearby, from seven o’clock in the morning. Naji and Fatima hunkered down beside their house’s interior walls, trying not to get hit.




When the initial aerial attacks abated, her daughter came with her four-year old son Amir. She told them she could not find her husband. Later reports by friends confirmed they have lost him to the Israeli attacks.




Refugees in the Philippines




Fatima and Naji did not want to leave Gaza at first. But as soon as stores could no longer open, electricity and water were cut off, they agreed to be repatriated to the Philippines via Egypt.




“We were among the third batch of Gazan refugees that flew to the Philippines a month and a half since the Israeli siege. We left on November 9 and arrived in Manila on November 14 of that year,” Fatima

author: Kodao Productions
title: Ignorant of History or Indifferent to Genocide?
content:
By 

Ina Alleco Silverio




The expectation that public figures must adhere to standard protocols of diplomatic engagement—meeting foreign envoys, exchanging pleasantries, and invoking the polite fiction and illusion of international respectability—collapses when applied to a state accused of ongoing, well-documented genocide and ecocide.




When a government actively violates the foundational conventions of human existence, conventional diplomacy stops being neutral; it becomes complicity. Upholding “decorum” or cultural norms like “pakikisama” in the presence of an official representative of such a state turns ethics into a hollow performance. It prioritizes institutional comfort over human survival, treating mass atrocities as mere disagreements in foreign policy rather than absolute moral crises.




True moral clarity requires a fundamental shift in how we understand diplomatic behavior!




There is an obvious difference, but a thin line between complicity and neutrality. Traditional diplomacy assumes that meeting an ambassador signals openness or dialogue. In the context of annihilation, however, normalization grants impunity. Refusing such meetings is not a failure of diplomacy; it is a necessary boundary-setting that rejects the sanitization of war crimes.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Leandro Leviste’s arrest order explained
content:
A local court ordered the arrest of one of the country’s youngest and richest legislators over alleged alleged failures to put up solar energy farms in accordance with a congressional franchise awarded in 2019.




Makati City Regional Trial Court Branch 235 issued a warrant of arrest against Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste on Monday, October 5, for allegedly violating the country’s Public Service Act (PSA). The warrant set Leviste’s bail at P72,000.




Leviste, however, is in Europe in an extended and unexplained absence from his duties as a member of the House of Representatives .




What is Leviste accused of?




Leviste is the founder of the Solar Para sa Bayan (Solar for the People) Corporation, granted a 25-year franchise to construct, install, establish, operate, and maintain solar-powered generation facilities and mini-grid systems in the Philippines. His company promised to supply affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity to underserved areas in the Philippines.




The company, however, failed to deliver, resulting in cancelled service contracts and billions of pesos in government penalties, the Department of Energy (DOE) reported.

author: Kodao Productions
title: How the Al-Aqsa Flood Shattered the Two-State Solution
content:
By 

Prof.

 

Sarah Raymundo




Marking three years since Operation Al-Aqsa Flood requires confronting how October 7 shattered the foundational ideological facade of modern imperialist diplomacy: the two-state solution.




Far from being a mere military escalation, the Flood operated as a decisive historical rupture that definitively broke the illusion that occupation could be perpetually managed through endless diplomatic process. It shattered the false premise that a people under genocidal  foreign domination could be pacified by paper accords built on the systematic erasure of history.




Where imperial diplomacy attempts to reduce occupation to a manageable border dispute, the underlying reality has been laid bare: the Palestinian question is fundamentally a struggle for national liberation against settler-colonialism, driven by the historic necessity of an oppressed nation to achieve emancipation by all means necessary, including armed resistance.




Even comprador regimes thoroughly integrated into the US-Israeli orbit are occasionally forced to acknowledge the weight of global outrage. The Philippine state—despite its active complicity in Israeli settler-colonialism through agricultural, economic, and military-cultural exchanges—joined the historic walkout at the UN General Assembly during Netanyahu’s address.

title: Duterte plot vs Marcos Jr. never stopped
content:
For more than two years, the Duterte political warlord dynasty never stopped plotting to oust the administration of Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and it came after Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio, an unknown quantity before she was pushed to run for vice president in 2022, hatched a scheme to force Marcos Jr. to quit and hand over political power to her as if it were candy. There was no rhyme or reason for this but it falls squarely on a bigger plot, which is to hand over to China all the maritime features in the South China Sea (SCS) and the West Philippine Sea (WPS) that Beijing covets.




This is the bigger context of the *scurrilous canard dished out by Rodrigo Duterte in July 2016, when the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) trashed China’s historical claim to Bajo de Masinloc, ruling that a feature nearly 1,000 kilometers from China was never possessed or occupied by Beijing for centuries, and, consequently, it could not invoke sovereign rights over it. Moreover, the nine-dash line calligraphy in 1947 done by a Chinese oceanographer on board an US Coast Guard cutter cannot qualify as a historical document. China has been claiming that Chinese mariners “discovered” the shoal 2,000 years ago and surveyed and mapped during the Song dynasty (960 AD-1279 AD.) title: Dubious China ties of Sara, Manases
content:
The Chinese Embassy may protest to high heavens that the P150-million it “donated” to a foundation headed by Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio was meant to “help” build classrooms in Davao City, but the Chinese corporations in Hong Kong and Southern China will be hard put proving that they were just buying banana chips from Cale 88, which appears to a small enterprise with a work force that is not even a dozen but scored a huge windfall of P1.25-billion from 2022 to 2025. This cannot be consistent with a business that paid an annual income tax that is a tad higher than P10,000. Moreover, Manases Carpio mysteriously disappeared as a stockholder with 47% equity when Sara was investigated and impeached. It turned out that another company also owned by the Dutertes “bought” Carpio’s interest.




Surely, Cale 88 Foods could not have shipped boatloads of banana chips to China with the few workers that it had. Most likely, and this is assuming that Cale 88 Foods were a legitimate food manufacturer, the venture could have bought huge volumes of banana chips from other companies in Tagum, Panabo (where prison labor can be exploited to the hilt) and other areas still free from the ravages of *fusarium wilt, particularly Tropical Race 4, and sent them to China. author: Kodao Productions
title: Exhibit on Palestinian heritage, struggle opens in UP
content:
An art exhibit opened at the University of the Philippines (UP) this week celebrating Palestinian Heritage Day on Wednesday, also Al-Aqsa Flood’s third anniversary. A selection of photographs, crafts, and devotional objects are on display at UP’s-College of Fine Arts (CFA) Art Gallery representing Palestinian way of life and struggle against Zionist occupation and genocide.




Palestinian Ambassador to the Philippines Mounir Anastas and UP President Angelo Jimenez opened the month-long exhibit entitled “Palestine: Living Heritage, Enduring Steadfastness,” offering visitors a direct connection to the nation’s enduring cultural traditions.




Photographs of historic sites across the West Bank are juxtaposed alongside images of Gaza’s heritage sites before and after their destruction by Israeli occupation forces.




Ambassador Anastas acted as the exhibit’s first guide, explaining traditional Palestinian arts, ranging from embroidery, painting, and devotional items. He expressed appreciation to the university and its Office of International Linkages as well as the CFA for their commitment to cultural preservation, education, and international solidarity.

title: Sara Duterte’s unexplained wealth and the AMLC’s incompetence
content:
By 

Atty. Ephraim B. Cortez

 / President, 

National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers




The purpose of impeachment proceedings is to determine the fitness of an impeachable officer to hold office. In the case of Sara Duterte, she is accused of betrayal of public trust, among other things, for amassing unexplained wealth.




The unexplained wealth includes monies transacted through the banking system, for which transactions were flagged and reported by banking institutions to the AMLC as covered or suspicious transactions.




As testified by the AMLC representative, their registry includes 666 covered transaction reports and 55 suspicious transaction reports involving billions of pesos transacted through the bank accounts of Sara Duterte and her husband.




The AMLC received 34 suspicious transaction reports involving transactions related to the Vice President’s bank account, while 30 suspicious transactions were attributed to Mans Carpio’s account.




These suspicious transaction reports have far-reaching implications. Aside from proving that Duterte and her spouse received income that was not duly reported in her SALN as required by law, and proving that she betrayed public trust, these transactions may indicate the commission of a crime.

title: Chinese teachers leaving in droves: Victims of inter-imperialist propaganda?
content:
About 150 Chinese teachers have begun leaving the Philippines in batches since last week, worried about their safety in a country that has had Chinese schools that are as old as 127 years.




The Chinese Embassy in Manila and the Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc. (FFCCCII) on Saturday said the foreign teachers were asked by their families to leave the Philippines for their safety.




The exodus came after a purported US security expert raised questions about the Chinese teachers’ true intentions in the country.




Ray Powell, founder and director of SeaLight, an initiative connected with Stanford University’s Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation, wrote last July that China’s Jinan University was involved in training Chinese-language teachers for schools in the Philippines.




Powell alleged their deployment to the Philippines had been directed by the Chinese Communist Party.




Philippine defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. echoed Powell’s warning, urging public vigilance regarding China-linked cultural and educational exchange programs and alleging that Jinan University “spreads fake news” by claiming that the Philippine northernmost province of Batanes belongs to China.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Pathetic Sara defense
content:
The defense lawyers of Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio appear to be having the worst time seeking to prevent lawyer Ronel Buenaventura, the executive director of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), from confirming the foreign currency deposits of the impeached vice president and her husband, Atty. Manases Carpio. Objecting to Buenaventura’s testimony, Sara’s lawyers invoked the confidentiality of dollar accounts under Republic Act No. 6426 (RA 6426), or the Foreign Currency Deposit Act (FCDA), arguing that AMLC cannot disclose any such information during the impeachment trial.




Presiding officer Chiz Escudero nixed the argument, explaining that confidentiality provision RA 6426 wilts when read within the context of the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), which compels banks to submit covered transaction reports (CTRs) and suspicious transaction reports (STRs) to the AMLC. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas regulations likewise torpedoed the defense argument as the absolute confidentiality of foreign-currency deposits is irrelevant to institutions that report such deposits to the AMLC through CTRs and STRs.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Migrant leader asks OWWA to review airport OFW Lounge policy
content:
Migrante International chairman emeritus Garry Martinez questioned Overseas Workers Welfare Administration’s (OWWA) rules on its Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW) Lounge at Manila International Airport after a distressed returning Filipina was turned away on Saturday.




A Filipina worker from Dubai has gone viral online, sparking a spirited debate on assistance given by the agency to departing and returning expatriates.




In an emotional video on Facebook, Remy Ropero Santos said she tried to enter the lounge at to find a place to stay and have something to eat.




In her video, Santos said she had no money on her as she could only withdraw the morning after of her arrival. Only then could she buy bus and boat tickets so she continue with her journey home, she added.




She tried explaining to lounge personnel she did not have a connecting flight as there are no airlines to her province, but was still rejected. Santos is on her way home to Sibuyan Island in Romblon, Province after spending two years in Dubai. Previously, she worked in Kuwait for six years.




The lounge, operated by the Philippine Overseas Welfare Administration (OWWA), is a dedicated area for departing OFWs or those with connecting domestic flights.




She said the lounge’s denial of her request to enter and eat is Philippine government’s mistreatment of OFWs like her.
